title: prefill-decode: chunked speculative prefill + stage overlap + KV scheduler optimizations
author: Ethan Chen
release_notes: Performance: Combined chunked speculative prefill, stage-overlap, and KV scheduler heuristics reduce tail latency and increase throughput for long-sequence, high-concurrency workloads. No API changes.
description: Motivation: Prefill and decode stages have historically been serialized which limits end-to-end throughput on long-context workloads and increases tail latency when KV cache miss rates spike. This PR implements three complementary runtime optimizations: 1) chunked prefill path that breaks long prefills into cacheable chunks to reduce peak memory pressure; 2) speculative prefill where we precompute likely KV cache entries for common prefix continuations and opportunistically populate GPU-resident KV stores; 3) a stage-overlap scheduler that allows prefill decode stages to execute in pipeline overlap when resource and data dependencies permit. Combined with a KV-aware scheduler heuristic that prioritizes requests with high cache-miss cost, these changes improve utilization and reduce per-token latency. Design: Chunked prefill splits the input sequence into configurable chunk_size windows and emits intermediate KV checkpoints. Speculative prefill uses a lightweight predictor trained on recent request traces (small n-gram fallback) to generate candidate continuation tokens; speculative KV writes are marked with a TTL and roll back on mismatch. Stage-overlap scheduler introduces an execution state machine enabling prefill tasks to yield to in-flight decode tasks and resume once dependencies are satisfied. The KV scheduler adds scoring based on estimated cache miss penalty and GPU memory pressure to decide placement and preemption. Safety and correctness: Speculative writes are strictly idempotent and isolated; rollback path is implemented and tested. Chunked prefill preserves exact outputs by reconstructing attention causal masks across chunk boundaries. Performance: Benchmarks on p4d.24xlarge with Llama-like 32k context show end-to-end latency improvements of 8-14% for 8k-32k prefills and speculative-chunking increases throughput by up to 1.6x under 80% concurrent load in synthetic microbenchmarks. KV-aware scheduling reduces 95th percentile latency by ~20% in mixed workload scenarios with high cache churn. Testing: Unit tests added for chunking, speculative KV lifecycle, and scheduler state transitions. Integration tests run against the runtime harness and the perf-canary infra. Benchmarks included under benchmark-lab. Rollout plan: feature flagged and gated by runtime flag prefill_pipeline_v2; gradual rollout with canary on dedicated pools, monitor token-level latencies, KV hit rates, and GC pressure. Related work: builds on previous prefill-decode overlap PRs and kernel scheduler work (see linked PRs). Impact: runtime throughput and latency improvements without protocol changes. Merge notes: squash-merged after CI flaps addressed; no customer-facing API changes.
